title: implement 1D convolutions

atoms.evidence: ow = 1 + (w - kw) // stride — full formula with stride; padding accounted for by pre-padding x rather than entering the formula
s_b, s_ic, s_w = x_padded.stride() — uses padded tensor's strides (which after pad are contiguous again because new_full allocates fresh)
x_strided = x_padded.as_strided(size=(b, ic, ow, kw), stride=(s_b, s_ic, s_w * stride, s_w))
einops.einsum(x_strided, weights, 'b ic ow kw, oc ic kw -> b oc ow')
extends 0_2_18 conv1d_minimal with stride and padding

x_padded = pad1d(x, left=padding, right=padding, pad_value=0) — first line of function; hint explicitly says 'replace x with the padded version of x so you don't have to worry about padding in the formula'
stride is a kwarg; new stride in as_strided is (s_w * stride) for the window-position dim — exactly the 'skip by stride elements between windows' trick shown in the hint diagram

notes: 8-atom exercise — densest conv exercise. First firing of conv-padding-zero and conv-stride-downsample as load-bearing (both were anticipated by the seed). The composition 'pre-pad-then-window-then-stride' is the canonical full-conv recipe — all four conv-mechanics atoms (output-shape, windowing, channel-sum, padding) plus stride co-fire.
